title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up the combinatorics of the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of the moduli spaces M_{g,ν}. An MD-graph (Mumford–Deligne graph) is a stable dual graph. It consists of a vertex set S, oriented arcs Ã (half-edges/oriented edges), a genus weight g: S→N and legs I→S. It must be connected and stable: 2g_β + (valence of β) ≥ 3.

On the previous page he defined 'generalized morphisms' of graphs. These amount to edge contractions G'→G, where B̃'⊂Ã' are the arcs that survive and C̃' = Ã'∖B̃' are the arcs sent to identities. He then began defining a 'morphism of generization' between MD-graphs G'→G: a generalized morphism plus a bijection of legs I'≅I, subject to conditions. This page lists those conditions.

(b) S'→S is surjective, B̃'→Ã is bijective, and the square I'→I over S'→S commutes. Hence B̃'⊔I' ≅ Ã⊔I compatibly with the maps to S. That is, the half-edges and legs at α are exactly the surviving half-edges and legs at the vertices above α.

(c) For each α∈S, form the fibre subgraph G'(α). Its vertices are the s'∈S' over α, and its arcs are the contracted arcs a'∈C̃' (those over id_α) whose origin, hence also endpoint, lies in S'_α. Give it legs I'_α ⊔ B̃'_α (marked points plus surviving half-edges leaving the fibre; note B̃'_α ≅ Ã_α) and genus g'|S'_α. This decorated graph must be an MD-graph: connected and stable.

Grothendieck notes that stability is automatic. The 'order' (valence) of β in G'(α), counting the new legs, equals its valence in G'. So 2g'_β + card I'_β + card B̃'_β + (contracted half-edges at β) ≥ 3 follows from G' being an MD-graph. The crossed-out attempts compare this with weaker or stronger variants, e.g. using B̃'_β alone, which would be a genuinely stronger and wrong requirement.

(d) The genus of the fibre equals the weight of α: Σ_{β∈S'_α} g'_β + h_1(G'(α)) = g_α.

In modern terms, G'→G is a morphism in the category of stable graphs (contraction). Each vertex α of G of type (g_α, n_α), with n_α = card I_α + card Ã_α, has as fibre a stable graph of type (g_α, n_α). This encodes that the stratum of G' lies in the closure of the stratum of G, and locally looks like a boundary stratum of ∏_α M̄_{g_α,n_α}. The next page restates the conditions in a form independent of the fibre MD-structure (surjectivity, bijectivity, connectedness of fibres, leg count, genus formula) and deletes the redundant stability condition.
errors: In (d) the page writes G(α) (both 'MD-graphe G(α)' and 'h_1(G(α))'); it should be the fibre graph G'(α), as the next page confirms. This is a notational slip.

The several crossed-out stability conditions show hesitation over which valence to use. The final version, valence of β in G'(α) including the legs I'_β ⊔ B̃'_β, is correct and automatically satisfied, as he notes and as the next page confirms by deleting 4°.

ideas.what: Morphisms of stable (MD) graphs as contractions, with leg bijection and fibrewise conditions; fibres of a contraction over each vertex are stable graphs of type (g_α, n_α) with genus additivity g_α = Σ g'_β + h_1.
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs / contraction morphisms (modular operad combinatorics, boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); formalized by Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the stratification at infinity of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower but does not give this formalism.

ideas.what: Observation that the fibre stability condition is automatic from stability of G', since fibre valence with new legs equals the original valence.
ideas.modern_name: Stability of vertex-fibres of a graph contraction

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard bookkeeping of contractions of stable dual graphs (the poset of boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}). It is now textbook, via Getzler–Kapranov and ACG. Historically mildly interesting as an independent formalization, but there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: In (d), 'h_1(G(α))' and 'MD-graphe G(α)' are as written on the page but should mathematically be G'(α).
'g_α : S'_α → N induit par g'' should be read as g'_α (restriction of g'); the subscript is ambiguous in the image.
The marginal note reads roughly: 'NB B̃'_α est l'ensemble des a'∈B̃' dont l'origine se trouve dans S'_α, i.e. B̃'_α ≅ Ã_α', which matches the transcription.
